title: The Fog Show
logline: The laundry-line shadow theater premieres tonight. Nimbus's stage-fright fog keeps covering the screen. The show is saved by writing the fog into the play.
starting_goal: Perform the shadow show for the garden's inhabitants
friction_source: The performer's nerves physically obscure the performance
character_want: Nimbus: wanted — the audience (snail, birds, the echo's listeners) is abstract and therefore terrifying
power_usage: Stage-fright fog rolls across the shadow screen; only the leak can produce the problem and the final effect
escalation: Escalation by kind: rehearsal calm -> curtain-time fog -> an intermission walk -> the rewrite where the monster IN the play arrives in fog, on purpose, to gasps
emotional_beat: The fog-monster gets the biggest gasp of the night; Nimbus takes a bow still fogging slightly, which reads as a special effect and also as courage
rewatch_detail: The fog's first 'accidental' shape is the same monster silhouette used in the finale — planted
distinctness_note: Stage fright solved by dramaturgy; the leak promoted from flaw to effect within the fiction

title: The Recital
logline: Grass-hum and reed-whistle duet, performed for the board's listeners. This time the stage fright is Pip's: his instrument needs his breath, and his breath is busy being scared.
starting_goal: Perform the duet at the garden recital
friction_source: A body-based instrument fails exactly when the body tenses
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — a public failure of skill, not of plan, is his un-rehearsed scenario
power_usage: Nimbus's reed-whistle is gust-driven and nerves-proof; the contrast is the lesson, not the gag
escalation: Escalation by kind: rehearsal schedules -> breathing drills -> Pip's squeaking first note, rescued by Nimbus holding the melody until Pip's breath returns
emotional_beat: The recital ends with the duet played once more, just for the two of them, better than the public one
rewatch_detail: Pip's rehearsal chart shows his best practice was at dawn, alone — the clue to the final scene's timing
distinctness_note: Stage fright assigned to the planner; rescue delivered by the expressive one — inversion honored

title: The Kite Ballet, Conducted
logline: A choreographed kite dance for community day. The world's breeze improvises mid-performance. The show becomes a duet between plan and sky, with Nimbus conducting, not powering.
starting_goal: Perform the planned kite ballet
friction_source: A live environment that does not attend rehearsals
character_want: Both: wanted — the show is their gift to the community; improvisation feels like losing the gift's wrapping
power_usage: None — the wind is the world's; Nimbus reads it and translates for Pip, which is skill, not power
escalation: Escalation by kind: figure one (perfect) -> figure two (the breeze solos) -> abandoning the score and conducting the breeze that exists, arms wide
emotional_beat: The crowd's applause (offscreen clatter of the stall pans) is for the improvisation; the program is re-titled 'Kite and Sky'
rewatch_detail: The breeze's improvisations match the laundry line's behavior all episode — forecastable on second viewing
distinctness_note: The cloud character as conductor of weather he does not make; performance with the world as partner

title: Duet With the Delay
logline: The echoing hill answers two beats late. A call-and-response concert means performing with a partner who is always yourself, late. Keeping time with your own echo is the whole skill.
starting_goal: Perform a call-and-response piece with the echo hill
friction_source: The duet partner is the performer's own delayed self
character_want: Nimbus: wanted — the echo is his favorite audience; Pip: competent-wanted — the delay is a solvable rhythm problem, surely
causal_detail: Delayed-feedback coordination: performing in sync with a fixed acoustic delay
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: simple calls -> overlapping rounds that tangle -> writing the delay INTO the piece so the echo completes each line on time
emotional_beat: The finished piece only exists with the hill; it cannot be performed anywhere else, and that is why it is theirs
rewatch_detail: The delay interval is consistent all episode; a child can clap along correctly by the finale
distinctness_note: The responsive world as musical partner with fixed physics; composition as adaptation

title: Being Pip for a Morning
logline: Nimbus performs Pip's morning routine exactly: map-check, tidy, tea. It is loving, accurate, and unbearable to watch. Pip meets himself from the outside.
starting_goal: Nimbus wants to try Pip's morning routine to understand it
friction_source: A faithful mirror is more uncomfortable than a funhouse one
character_want: Pip: wanted — seeing his rituals performed asks whether they are care or cage; Nimbus: needed — understanding the ritual is respecting it
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: copied map-check -> copied label-straightening -> Nimbus adding one item to the map: 'watch Nimbus be Pip', which breaks the bit and opens the talk
emotional_beat: Pip keeps the routines and drops the one that was only ever armor; Nimbus's imitation earns a place in the map margin
rewatch_detail: Nimbus's copy is exact down to the teaspoon orientation — checkable against the opening scene
distinctness_note: Imitation as empathy instrument; the mirrored character edits himself, gently

title: The Earthbound Float-Wave
logline: Pip learns Nimbus's float-wave greeting. Without floating, it is mostly jumping. The greeting mutates until it is half hover, half hop, and entirely theirs.
starting_goal: Pip wants to greet Nimbus in Nimbus's own gesture language
friction_source: A gesture built for buoyancy performed by a grounded body
character_want: Pip: wanted — speaking the friend's language is a belonging offering; Nimbus: needed — being imitated is being read back
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: direct copy (jump) -> assisted copy (trampoline of the springy branch) -> fusion greeting: Pip's hop plus Nimbus's dip, in counterpoint
emotional_beat: The fused greeting is drilled at the fence and becomes the show's recurring hello, visible from then on
rewatch_detail: The greeting's final form appears half-finished in the middle scenes' backgrounds as practice
distinctness_note: A behavioral signature is invented ON SCREEN — the series' hello is born inside an episode

title: Teaching the Hill
logline: If the echo repeats what it hears, can it be taught new sounds? Call-and-response practice for days. The day the hill answers with something untaught, the investigation finds reeds and wind.
starting_goal: Teach the echo hill a new call
friction_source: A responsive world that imitates but cannot learn — until the day it seems to
character_want: Nimbus: wanted — the hill is his voice's friend; Pip: competent-wanted — the anomaly must have a cause
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: drills -> apparent progress -> the untaught answer (wonder, briefly) -> the reed-and-wind explanation, which is better than magic because it can be played again
emotional_beat: The hill keeps its repertoire of echoes; the reeds get a thank-you concert; wonder survives the explanation
rewatch_detail: The reeds sway audibly in every 'learning' scene — the hidden third musician
distinctness_note: A fantasy hypothesis (the hill learns) is proposed by the story and retired by observation — the science-boundary stance in miniature

title: Copy Day
logline: Copy Day rules: each must do everything the other does, all day. Planning collapses without a planner; floating collapses without a floater. Both apologize to their own methods by dinner.
starting_goal: Spend one full day copying each other
friction_source: Two complete systems, each unusable by the other
character_want: Both: wanted — the game is admiration; the cost is discovering how much of the other is unreplicable
power_usage: Nimbus's drizzle copies Pip's watering can poorly; the mismatch is comic but removable
escalation: Escalation by kind: morning routines -> chores -> each making the other's signature mistake ON PURPOSE to stay in the game
emotional_beat: Copy Day is retired undefeated; both keep one borrowed gesture each, permanently
rewatch_detail: The borrowed gestures persist in later episodes — the episode's artifacts enter the series' behavior set
distinctness_note: Role-reversal played as admiration rather than competition; the residue becomes permanent behavior

title: Surprising a Snail
logline: The snail has lived in the garden one whole year. A surprise party is prepared at human speed and received at snail speed. The surprise takes three days to land.
starting_goal: Throw a surprise anniversary for the snail
friction_source: The honored guest operates on a timescale that defuses all surprise mechanics
character_want: Both: needed — the snail is family; the party is a belonging bid toward a creature who cannot hurry
power_usage: A confetti of mist-droplets is planned; the timing problem exists with or without it
escalation: Escalation by kind: hidden decorations -> the guest approaching at a leaf per hour -> holding the surprise pose across a nap, a meal, and a small internal crisis
emotional_beat: The snail arrives at the decorations on day three and stops — which for a snail is gasping; the party is declared to have worked exactly as planned
rewatch_detail: The snail's approach is trackable across the entire episode against background pebbles
distinctness_note: Surprise mechanics versus the slowest guest; the celebration adapts to the celebrated

title: The Surprise That Needed a Leak
logline: Nimbus cannot keep secrets — his drip betrays them. So Pip designs a surprise that only works BY leaking: the drip trail is the invitation, and finding it early is the game.
starting_goal: Design a surprise that survives Nimbus's inability to hide feelings
friction_source: A friend whose body announces secrets, and a ritual that requires secrecy
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — designing AROUND the leak is the puzzle; Nimbus: wanted — being known this well is being loved this well
power_usage: The leak is the delivery channel of the invitation; the premise inverts the usual concealment problem
escalation: Escalation by kind: decoy drip trail -> real trail disguised as accident -> Nimbus discovering the design and leaking ON PURPOSE, which is the first controllable leak of the series
emotional_beat: The surprise (a picnic at the drip trail's end) lands on time; the intentional leak is celebrated as a new skill, not cured as a flaw
rewatch_detail: The decoy and real trails diverge at the old fence — a verifiable fork for rewatchers
distinctness_note: The defining flaw is promoted to a feature BY DESIGN of the friend — the friendship thesis in one mechanism

title: The Mystery Seeds
logline: The pen-pal mails unlabeled seeds. What will they be? Planting a question mark and waiting weeks for the answer. The reveal: red poppies, exactly the ones on Pip's favorite page.
starting_goal: Plant the unknown seeds and discover what they are
friction_source: A gift whose content is delayed by biology
character_want: Both: wanted — the pen-pal chose this for them; the waiting is threaded with being thought of
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: guessing games -> sprout taxonomy (wrong) -> bud stake-out -> the first red petal arriving when nobody is looking, as answers do
emotional_beat: The poppies match Pip's favorite page; the reply drawing mailed back shows the poppies drawn AS question marks that bloomed
rewatch_detail: The favorite-page flower is visible in Pip's book in several earlier episodes
distinctness_note: Delayed reveal powered by correspondence and botany; the surprise belongs to time, not to a trick

title: The First-Rain Anniversary
logline: They celebrate the day Nimbus first rained for the garden — except nobody wrote down the date. Choosing a date honestly, then celebrating water in the middle of the world's own rain.
starting_goal: Hold the first-rain anniversary celebration
friction_source: A ritual without a record; then a venue full of the very thing being celebrated
character_want: Nimbus: wanted — the anniversary is proof he belongs in the garden's history; Pip: competent-wanted — a missing record is a personal wound
power_usage: None; the day-of rain is the world's
escalation: Escalation by kind: date forensics -> choosing 'today, every year' -> the outdoor party migrating under the shelter, where rain ON the shelter roof becomes the soundtrack
emotional_beat: The ritual is fixed as 'the first rain after the poppies bloom' — a date the garden keeps better than any calendar
rewatch_detail: The poppy bloom cross-references the mystery-seeds episode; the ritual date is computable by rewatchers
distinctness_note: A ritual invented to be weather-proof by being weather-defined; calendar logic replaced by phenology

title: The Hundredth Entry
logline: The map's hundredth entry must be worthy. Nothing worthy happens all day; worthy things are chased and scare off. The entry, finally: 'the day we tried too hard'.
starting_goal: Find a worthy event for the map's hundredth entry
friction_source: Milestone pressure repels the unscripted good
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — the record is his legacy; a mundane hundredth feels like a crack in it
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: candidate list -> event-hunting with nets and hope -> scaring off three perfectly good ordinary moments by hunting them
emotional_beat: The honest entry is written; Nimbus adds a drawing of Pip writing it — the hundredth entry is itself commemorated as a failure of ceremony
rewatch_detail: The three scared-off moments are each visible starting to happen in the background of earlier scenes
distinctness_note: Meta-episode about the record-keeping itself; the milestone celebrates ordinariness honestly

title: Lantern Boats at Dusk
logline: For the pen-pal: a fleet of leaf-lantern boats sent down the stream at dusk. Every boat must survive the bend. The reply note: 'they arrived like stars'.
starting_goal: Send a lantern fleet downstream to arrive at dusk
friction_source: Fragile lights, moving water, and a hard sunset deadline
character_want: Both: wanted — the gift is beauty delivered by physics; failure is just darkness, but the heart wants stars
power_usage: One gentle gust frees a snagged lantern; the fleet sails on the world's water regardless
escalation: Escalation by kind: single test boat (sinks, candle out, recovered) -> ballast lessons from the cargo experiment -> the fleet launched in silence and followed by ear
emotional_beat: The reply drawing shows the lanterns arriving; the two sit by the dark stream, which briefly carries their reflection-light instead
rewatch_detail: The test boat's failure teaches the fix visible in the fleet; the physics is consistent and checkable
distinctness_note: A beauty-delivery engineering episode; payoff arrives by mail, not on screen — trust in the world rewarded

title: The Depth Chart and the Rain Practice
logline: Pip's goal today: finish the stream depth chart. Nimbus's goal today: practice rain-rhythms for the pen-pal's answer. Both goals are legitimate. Both need the same bank at the same time.
starting_goal: Each wants to complete his own project at the stream bank
friction_source: Two solo goals colliding in one place; neither goal is foolish
character_want: Both: wanted — the day promised each of them a finished thing
power_usage: Rhythm-practice rain keeps spotting the chart paper; the interference is the practice itself
escalation: Escalation by kind: spatial split (half the bank each) -> the splash radius respects no borders -> a rain schedule alternating with a measuring schedule, negotiated like nations
emotional_beat: The treaty works; both finish at dusk; the chart's margin carries one rain-spot, labeled 'Nimbus was here, practicing'
rewatch_detail: The negotiation's terms are posted on the boathouse door and obeyed in later episodes
distinctness_note: Neither goal yields morally; scheduling as diplomacy between equals

title: The Solo Errand
logline: Nimbus's first solo errand: return the borrowed bowl to the stall. Pip's goal for the day is harder: do not escort him. Both succeed. The reunion hum is loud.
starting_goal: Nimbus wants to do the errand alone; Pip wants to let him
friction_source: Independence requires one to go and the other to stay
character_want: Nimbus: wanted — capability witnessed by himself; Pip: needed — suppressing escort-care without suppressing love
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: goodbye protocol -> a 'small' farewell kit of maps, signals, and four snacks -> Pip tracking the errand by distant drizzle-sight and pretending to garden
emotional_beat: The bowl returns empty (muffins happened); the errand's report is given in full ceremony; the farewell kit is unpacked, unused, with pride
rewatch_detail: Pip's garden work during the errand is all done facing the wrong direction — checkable
distinctness_note: Independence episode where the staying character carries the harder arc

title: The History Book and Today
logline: Pip is writing the garden's history. Nimbus's plan for today is play. Work versus play, until the book's best page turns out to be the one about today.
starting_goal: Pip wants a writing day; Nimbus wants a play day
friction_source: Two day-designs sharing one friendship
character_want: Pip: wanted — the book is his gift to the future; Nimbus: needed — a friend absorbed in the past is a friend half-elsewhere
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: quiet-corner agreements -> Nimbus's solo games migrating closer -> the leaf-fight ambush that no historian can document from inside
emotional_beat: The history book gains its first present-tense page: 'today we played'; the page is illustrated by both, badly, together
rewatch_detail: The book's visible pages throughout are summaries of actual earlier episodes
distinctness_note: Work-play tension resolved by discovering they are the same material; the artifact includes the conflict

title: Nimbus Runs the Day
logline: Nimbus plans the whole day: schedule, checklist, contingencies. His plan is good. His plan is also exhausting — for him. Pip floats through it beautifully and a little guiltily.
starting_goal: Nimbus wants to run one full day by plan, Pip-style
friction_source: Planning as care-work is invisible until you carry it
character_want: Nimbus: wanted — proving he can; Pip: wanted — being cared-for without managing the care is foreign and slightly alarming
power_usage: None required; the schedule's weather items are assigned to him by himself, which is the joke's structure
escalation: Escalation by kind: morning schedule (works) -> contingency cascade at lunch -> the 3pm entry that just reads 'lie down', obeyed by both
emotional_beat: Dinner is unplanned on purpose; the planning job becomes shared by treaty, with Nimbus keeping the checklist he invented: 'also rest'
rewatch_detail: Nimbus's checklist is fully readable and each item is visibly checked or heroically abandoned
distinctness_note: Role-reversal that generates respect for the role rather than ridicule of it

title: The Last Muffin Debate
logline: One muffin left. Split it? Give it away? Save it for a day that deserves it? Three rounds of debate, escalating principles, solved by a fourth party arriving at snail speed.
starting_goal: Decide the last muffin's fate fairly
friction_source: Every fair rule they invent has an exception they also invented
character_want: Both: wanted — each wants the other to have it more than he wants it, and wants it
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: halving (crumbs inequality) -> merit arguments -> a formal debate with the snail as accidental judge by arrival
emotional_beat: Three-way split, snail's share in crumbs; the debate rules are kept as 'Muffin Law' on the boathouse door
rewatch_detail: The snail's approach begins in scene one; its arrival time is computable from its trail
distinctness_note: Fairness philosophy at crumb scale; the third force adjudicates by simply existing slowly

title: Bird or Hat
logline: The pen-pal's drawing is ambiguous: bird, or hat? Instead of guessing, the pair invents the question protocol — and the answer (a bird in a hat) is better than either guess.
starting_goal: Find out what the pen-pal's drawing shows
friction_source: An ambiguous message across a slow channel
character_want: Both: competent-wanted — guessing wrong in a reply would be recorded forever
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: two interpretation camps, escalating evidence -> the question protocol drafted with official wording -> the reply settling it and delighting both camps
emotional_beat: The question protocol joins the signals chart; 'asking is allowed' is demonstrated as correspondence, not stated as lesson
rewatch_detail: The ambiguous drawing is shown plainly; both readings genuinely fit
distinctness_note: Clarification modeled as a tool you invent, not a weakness you hide

title: The Fog-Shuffled Morning
logline: The world's fog rearranges the morning: things emerge from the white in the wrong order. Pip narrates each shape confidently and wrongly. The fog lifts on a world slightly scrambled.
starting_goal: Navigate and inventory the garden through the fog
friction_source: Partial information invites confident wrongness
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — his world-knowledge should beat fog; it should not
power_usage: None — and Nimbus, asked if fog is 'his', says no: weather bigger than him belongs to the world
escalation: Escalation by kind: confident identifications (wrong) -> the drifted boat, the relocated sign, the snail atop the post -> a fog-day map correction session
emotional_beat: The corrections are entered in a new ink color: 'fog corrections'; the color is later used only for honest surprises
rewatch_detail: Every misidentified shape's true form is checkable against the pre-lift silhouette
distinctness_note: The world fogs on its own; Nimbus is explicitly not all weather — identity boundaries clarified in-fiction

title: One Rope, Two Jobs
logline: The kite needs its line. The boat needs its mooring. There is one good rope. Alternating days is tried; then a pulley share is invented: one rope, two jobs, in sequence.
starting_goal: Serve two needs with one rope
friction_source: A single resource allocated across time instead of across rivals
character_want: Both: competent-wanted — the elegant allocation is a shared trophy
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: simultaneous need discovered (kite up, boat loose) -> alternating days (weather-dependent grievance) -> the pulley sequence that lets one rope work both ends of the day
emotional_beat: The rope schedule is pinned; on wind-days the kite wins, on calm-days the boat — the world gets a vote, fairly
rewatch_detail: The world's vote is visible: each morning's flag direction decides the rope's job
distinctness_note: Time-division engineering with the environment as tiebreaker; distinct from the gift-plank collision

title: The Rain Director
logline: Today Pip directs the watering: he reads the garden, calls the timing, Nimbus rains on call. Pip's schedule says noon; the seedlings' faces say now. Reading beats scheduling.
starting_goal: Run the garden's watering day with Pip directing and Nimbus raining
friction_source: Command of the power by the non-powered; schedule versus observed need
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — directing rain is the closest he comes to weather; Nimbus: needed — rained-on-call risks feeling like plumbing
power_usage: Directed mild rain on request; the direction relationship is the experiment
escalation: Escalation by kind: noon schedule -> drooping seedlings on schedule's time, not theirs -> Pip learning to read leaf-posture and calling rain early, against the plan, correctly
emotional_beat: The schedule is replaced by a reading ritual: morning leaf-rounds, rain when the garden asks; the director credits the garden
rewatch_detail: Leaf-posture readings match the seedlings' actual states shown in close-up earlier
distinctness_note: Agency inversion: the powerless character commands the power and learns the observation skill

title: Raining Like the Sky
logline: Nimbus tries to rain like the world's big sky: all at once, everywhere. It goes grey, thin, wrong. His own drizzle — aimed, small, meant — is the better rain for being his.
starting_goal: Nimbus wants to water the whole garden like real sky-rain does
friction_source: Imitating a system a hundred times his size with a two-effect power set
character_want: Nimbus: needed — sky-rain is the admired professional; his drizzle feels junior
power_usage: Attempted wide rain exhausts him (cost rule) and under-serves each plant; his bounded drizzle is the craft answer
escalation: Escalation by kind: spread-thin rain (nothing wets) -> grey sag of overreach -> the row-by-row drizzle service, personal per plant, better than the sky's indifference
emotional_beat: The garden book records: 'sky rain: general. Nimbus rain: personal.' He reads it twice
rewatch_detail: Each plant's droop and recovery is individually animated across the comparison
distinctness_note: Self-acceptance through craft comparison; the bounded power's smallness is reframed as precision

title: The Spare Kite Goes Downstream
logline: The pen-pal has no kite. The pair owns two. Giving away the good spare is easy to say and hard to do; the send-off is a small ceremony; the reply drawing shows it flying.
starting_goal: Give the spare kite to the downstream friend
friction_source: Generosity versus attachment to the better of two
character_want: Both: wanted — the gift proves the friendship's reach; the cost is real and small, like all real gifts
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: choosing the spare (the good one? the GOOD one?) -> a farewell flight for the kite -> wrapping it with instructions, maps, and one tear wiped officially on both sleeves
emotional_beat: The reply drawing arrives: the kite over the downstream bridge; the remaining kite flies better, somehow, or so they agree to say
rewatch_detail: The kite's tail ribbon matches the fence ribbon from an earlier episode — the gift carries history
distinctness_note: Generosity with real cost and postal payoff; objects carry continuity across the community layer

title: The Icon Plans
logline: Pip's written plans mean nothing to a friend who reads weather. The pair invents pictogram plans: rain-drop icon, sun icon, snack icon. The rain icon is misread as tears once, memorably.
starting_goal: Invent a plan format both can read
friction_source: Two reading systems sharing one planning need
character_want: Both: wanted — a shared notation is a shared mind; the misreadings are the price of inventing it
power_usage: None required; the rain icon's resemblance to a tear drives the central misread gag
escalation: Escalation by kind: word plans (failed) -> icons (tears/rain confusion leads to an unnecessary comfort mission) -> the revised icon set with the official 'actual rain' vs 'feelings rain' distinction
emotional_beat: The icon set is pinned in the shed; the tears/rain confusion is never fully fixed and becomes their private joke glyph
rewatch_detail: The icon set appears on plans in all later episodes, evolving by accretion
distinctness_note: The series' own sparse-dialogue problem solved in-fiction by the characters; meta-fit without fourth wall

title: The Page the Wind Returned
logline: A map page lost to a gust weeks ago is returned by last night's wind — weathered, faded, changed. The old map cannot be re-used, so the archive is born: history, kept.
starting_goal: Decide what to do with the returned, weather-changed map page
friction_source: The recovered thing no longer matches the world it mapped
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — the current map is right; the old page is wrong; discarding it feels like discarding time
power_usage: None; both gusts were the world's
escalation: Escalation by kind: comparing old page to new world -> Pip's memory claiming the old page was perfect (it wasn't; evidence on screen) -> the archive box labeled 'how it was'
emotional_beat: The archive box gets its second item immediately: yesterday's dried leaf; history starts being kept on purpose
rewatch_detail: The lost page's disappearance was visible in the earlier wind-night episode — the loss was planted, the return pays it off
distinctness_note: Recovery without restoration; the found thing's value is as history, not as tool

title: Take One, Leave One
logline: The found-things board has a rule: take one, leave one. Today there are two treasures — a glass button and a brass whistle — and the rule allows only one home with them.
starting_goal: Choose one treasure under the take-one-leave-one rule
friction_source: A self-imposed fairness rule against genuine double desire
character_want: Both: wanted — the rule is theirs; breaking it privately would be invisible and unbearable
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: trial custody of both (one day each) -> criteria lists that keep tying -> the realization that the whistle calls birds and the button just sparkles, so the whistle stays for the garden's sake
emotional_beat: The button is left for the next finders with a tag: 'sparkles more than it looks'; choosing for the world, not the self, is the day's quiet trophy
rewatch_detail: The button reappears on the board in later episodes until an unknown finder finally takes it
distinctness_note: Choosing under a self-imposed rule; the deciding criterion is service to the world, not preference
